one: two (in counting, dates and numbers like 12)

There are three people in his family.
There are six apples on the table.
This piece of clothing is 100 yuan.
It is half past seven now.

one: prefix that makes ordinal numbers (第一 = first)
我有一个哥哥。: 今天是我学汉语的第一天。
Today is my first day of learning Chinese.
I ate half of this apple.
I want to buy some fruit.

one: a few, some (used after 这, 那, 哪, 有)
a little, a bit of something
I can speak a little Chinese.

one: a bit, somewhat (often about something you don't want)
It is a bit cold today.

我有一个哥哥。: 有的人喜欢喝茶，有的人喜欢喝牛奶。
Some people like tea, and some like milk.

How many people are in your family?

one: measure word for clothes and for matters
I want to buy a new piece of clothing.

one: measure word for family members (also: mouth)
There are four people in my family.

one: zhī: measure word for animals. zhǐ: only

I get up at seven o'clock.
My daughter is five years old.
